record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Computational Geometry
record.context_brief: Bipartite matching in bichromatic unit disk or square graphs
record.original_question: Given a red family and a blue family of unit disks, or of axis-parallel unit squares, in the plane, form the bipartite intersection graph whose vertices are all objects and whose edges connect only intersecting red-blue pairs. Can a maximum matching in this bipartite geometric intersection graph be found in near-linear time?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let R and B be two finite families of objects in the plane, where each object is either a closed unit disk or an axis-parallel closed unit square (with the same type used for both families). Form the bipartite intersection graph G = (R ∪ B, E), whose vertex set is R ∪ B and whose edge set consists of all pairs {r, b} with r ∈ R, b ∈ B such that r ∩ b ≠ ∅. A matching in G is a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges, and a maximum matching is one of largest cardinality.

Let n = |R| + |B|. Determine whether a maximum matching of G can be computed exactly in near-linear time, i.e., in time O(n · polylog n).
artifact.status_search_result: The current best known exact algorithms for maximum bipartite matching in unit disk intersection graphs run in roughly O(n^{3/2} polylog n) time (Efrat–Itai–Katz style algorithms, and recent improvements via Kaplan et al.'s dynamic nearest-neighbor data structures). Near-linear time algorithms are known only for constant-factor or (1−ε)-approximations, not for exact maximum matching. No publication establishing an exact near-linear-time algorithm (or a matching lower bound) for the bichromatic unit-disk or unit-square case appears in the literature, so the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Maximum Matchings in Geometric Intersection Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Efrat et al. show how to compute the maximum matching in bipartite unit disk graphs in O(n^{3/2} log n) time.
status_evidence.claim: The best known exact algorithm runs in O(n^{3/2} log n) time, not near-linear.

status_evidence.title: Approximation Algorithms for Maximum Matchings in Geometric Intersection Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: near linear approximation algorithm for the bipartite case
status_evidence.claim: Near-linear results are only for approximation, leaving the exact near-linear question open.
